vsm2.20:18.0: Strengthening of Comprehension in Forty Ways
vsm2.20:18.1:
Now, when the Blessed One was expounding conformity knowledge, he asked the question: “By means of what
forty aspects does he acquire liking that is in conformity?
vsm2.20:18.2: By means of what forty aspects does he enter into the certainty of rightness?” (P‘8).
vsm2.20:18.3:
In the answer to it comprehension of impermanence, etc., is set forth by him analytically in the way beginning:
“Seeing the five aggregates as impermanent, as painful, as a disease, a boil, a dart, a calamity, an affliction,
as alien, as disintegrating, as a plague, a disaster, a terror, a menace, as fickle, perishable, unenduring,
vsm2.20:18.4:
as no protection, no shelter, no refuge, as empty, vain, void, not-self, as a danger, as subject to change, as having no core,
as the root of calamity, as murderous, as due to be annihilated, as subject to cankers, as formed, as Māra’s bait,
vsm2.20:18.5:
as subject to birth, subject to ageing, subject to illness, subject to death, subject to sorrow,
subject to lamentation, subject to despair, as subject to defilement.
vsm2.20:18.6: Seeing the five aggregates as impermanent, he acquires liking that is in conformity.
vsm2.20:18.7:
And seeing that the cessation of the five aggregates is the permanent Nibbāna,
he enters into the certainty of rightness” (Paṭis II 238).
vsm2.20:18.8: So in order to strengthen that same comprehension of impermanence, pain, and not-self in the five aggregates,
vsm2.20:18.9: this meditator also comprehends these five aggregates by means of that kind of comprehension.
vsm2.20:19.1:
How does he do it? He does it by means of comprehension as impermanent, etc., stated specifically as follows:
He comprehends each aggregate as impermanent because of non-endlessness, and because of possession of a beginning and an end;
vsm2.20:19.2:
as painful because of oppression by rise and fall, and because of being the basis for pain; as a disease
because of having to be maintained by conditions, and because of being the root of disease;
vsm2.20:19.5: as disintegrating because of crumbling through sickness, ageing and death; as a plague because of bringing various kinds of ruin;
vsm2.20:19.7: as fickle because of fickle insecurity due to sickness, ageing and death, and to the worldly states of gain, etc.;
vsm2.20:19.8:
as perishable because of having the nature of perishing both by violence and naturally;
as unenduring because of collapsing on every occasion and because of lack of solidity;
vsm2.20:19.11: as not-self because of itself having no owner, etc.;
vsm2.20:19.13:
as subject to change because of having the nature of change in two ways, that is, through ageing and through death;
as having no core because of feebleness, and because of decaying soon like sapwood;
vsm2.20:19.14:
as the root of calamity because of being the cause of calamity; as murderous because of breaking faith like an enemy posing
as a friend; as due to be annihilated because their becoming disappears, and because their non-becoming comes about;
vsm2.20:19.15:
as subject to cankers because of being the proximate cause for cankers; as formed because of being formed by causes and conditions;
as Māra’s bait because of being the bait laid by the Māra of death and the Māra of defilement;
vsm2.20:19.16:
as subject to birth, to ageing, to illness, and to death because of having birth, ageing, illness and death as their nature;
as subject to sorrow, to lamentation and to despair because of being the cause of sorrow, lamentation and despair;
vsm2.20:19.17: as subject to defilement because of being the objective field of the defilements of craving, views and misconduct.
vsm2.20:20.1:
Now, there are fifty kinds of contemplation of impermanence here by taking the following ten in the case of each
aggregate: as impermanent, as disintegrating, as fickle, as perishable, as unenduring, as subject to change,
as having no core, as due to be annihilated, as formed, as subject to death.
vsm2.20:20.2:
There are twenty-five kinds of contemplation of not-self by taking the following five in the case of each
aggregate: as alien, as empty, as vain, as void, as not-self.
vsm2.20:20.3:
There are one hundred and twenty-five kinds of contemplation of pain by taking the rest
beginning with “as painful, as a disease” in the case of each aggregate.
vsm2.20:20.4:
So when a man comprehends the five aggregates by means of this comprehending as impermanent, etc., in its two hundred aspects,
his comprehending as impermanent, painful and not-self, which is called “inductive insight,” is strengthened.
vsm2.20:20.5: These in the first place are the directions for undertaking comprehension here in accordance with the method given in the texts.
vsm2.20:21.0: Nine Ways of Sharpening the Faculties, Etc.
vsm2.20:21.1:
While thus engaged in inductive insight, however, if it does not succeed, he should sharpen his faculties of faith,
etc., in the nine ways stated thus: “The faculties become sharp in nine ways: (1) he sees only the destruction of arisen formations;
vsm2.20:21.2:
(2) and in that occupation he makes sure of working carefully, (3) he makes sure of working perseveringly, (4) he makes
sure of working suitably, and (5) by apprehending the sign of concentration and (6) by balancing the enlightenment factors
vsm2.20:21.3: (7) he establishes disregard of body and life, (8) wherein he overcomes pain by renunciation and (9) by not stopping halfway.
vsm2.20:21.4:
He should avoid the seven unsuitable things in the way stated in the Description of the Earth Kasiṇa (IV.34) and cultivate
the seven suitable things, and he should comprehend the material at one time and the immaterial at another.
vsm2.20:22.1: While comprehending materiality he should see how materiality is generated
vsm2.20:23.1: Herein, the cessation of materiality is slow and its transformation ponderous,
vsm2.20:23.2: while the cessation of consciousness is swift and its transformation quick (light);
vsm2.20:23.3: hence it is said, “Bhikkhus, I see no other one thing
vsm2.20:23.4: that is so quickly transformed as the mind” (A I 10).
vsm2.20:24.1: For the life-continuum consciousness arises and ceases sixteen times while one material instant endures.
vsm2.20:24.2: With consciousness the instant of arising, instant of presence, and instant of dissolution are equal;
vsm2.20:24.3: but with materiality only the instants of arising and dissolution are quick like those of consciousness,
vsm2.20:24.4: while the instant of its presence is long and lasts while sixteen consciousnesses arise and cease.
vsm2.20:25.1:
With the prenascent physical heart-basis as its support, which has already reached
presence and arose at the rebirth-linking consciousness’s instant of arising,
vsm2.20:25.3:
With the prenascent physical basis as its support, which has already reached presence and arose
together with that second life-continuum consciousness,
vsm2.20:25.5: The occurrence of consciousness can be understood to happen in this way throughout life.
vsm2.20:25.6: But in one who is facing death, with a single prenascent physical heart-basis as their support, which has already reached presence,
vsm2.20:26.1: The materiality that arose at the instant of arising of the rebirth-linking consciousness
vsm2.20:26.2: ceases along with the sixteenth consciousness after the rebirth-linking consciousness.
vsm2.20:26.3: That arisen at the instant of presence ceases together with the instant of arising of the seventeenth.
vsm2.20:26.4: That arisen at the instant of its dissolution ceases on arriving at the instant of presence of the seventeenth.
vsm2.20:26.5: It goes on occurring thus for as long as the recurrence of births continues.
vsm2.20:26.6: Also, with the sevenfold continuity beginning with the eye decad of those apparitionally born,
vsm2.20:26.7: seventy instances of materiality occur in the same way.
vsm2.20:27.1:
(A) KAMMA-BORN MATERIALITY

Herein, as regards kamma-born materiality the analysis should be understood thus: (1) kamma,
vsm2.20:27.3: (3) what has kamma as its condition,
vsm2.20:27.4: (4) what is originated by consciousness that has kamma as its condition,
vsm2.20:27.5: (5) what is originated by nutriment that has kamma as its condition,
vsm2.20:27.6: (6) what is originated by temperature that has kamma as its condition (XI.111–14).
vsm2.20:28.1: Herein, (1) kamma is profitable and unprofitable volition.
vsm2.20:28.2:
(2) What is originated by kamma is the kamma-resultant aggregates and the seventy
instances of materiality beginning with the eye decad.
vsm2.20:28.3: (3) What has kamma as its condition is the same as the last
vsm2.20:28.4: since kamma is the condition that upholds what is originated by kamma.
vsm2.20:29.1: (4) What is originated by consciousness that has kamma as its condition is materiality originated by kamma-resultant consciousness.
vsm2.20:29.2: (5) What is originated by nutriment that has kamma as its condition is so called
vsm2.20:29.3:
since the nutritive essence that has reached presence in the instances of materiality
originated by kamma originates a further octad-with-nutritive-essence-as-eighth,
vsm2.20:29.4: and the nutritive essence there that has reached presence also originates a further one,
vsm2.20:29.5: and so it links up four or five occurrences of octads.
vsm2.20:29.6: (6) What is originated by temperature that has kamma as its condition is so called
vsm2.20:29.7:
since the kamma-born fire element that has reached presence originates
an octad-with-nutritive-essence-as-eighth, which is temperature-originated,
vsm2.20:29.8:
and the temperature in that originates a further octad-with-nutritive-essence-as-eighth, and so
it links up four or five occurrences of octads.
vsm2.20:29.9: This is how the generation of kamma-born materiality in the first place should be seen.
vsm2.20:30.1:
(B) CONSCIOUSNESS-BORN MATERIALITY

Also as regards the consciousness-born kinds, the analysis should be understood thus: (1) consciousness,
vsm2.20:30.3: (3) what has consciousness as its condition,
vsm2.20:30.4: (4) what is originated by nutriment that has consciousness as its condition,
vsm2.20:30.5: (5) what is originated by temperature that has consciousness as its condition.
vsm2.20:31.1: Herein, (1) consciousness is the eighty-nine kinds of consciousness. Among these:
vsm2.20:31.2:
> Consciousnesses thirty-two,
> And twenty-six, and nineteen too,
> Are reckoned to give birth to matter,
> Postures, also intimation;
> Sixteen kinds of consciousness
> Are reckoned to give birth to none.
vsm2.20:31.3:
As regards the sense sphere, thirty-two consciousnesses, namely, the eight profitable
consciousnesses ((1)–(8)), the twelve unprofitable ((22)–(33)),
vsm2.20:31.4:
the ten functional excluding the mind element ((71)–(80)), and the two direct-knowledge
consciousnesses as profitable and functional,
vsm2.20:31.5: give rise to materiality, to postures, and to intimation.
vsm2.20:31.6:
The twenty-six consciousnesses, namely, the ten of the fine-material sphere ((9)–(13),
(81)–(85)) and the eight of the immaterial sphere ((14)–(17), (86)–(89)) excluding the resultant in both cases,
vsm2.20:31.7: and the eight supramundane ((18)–(21), (66)–(69)), give rise to materiality, to postures but not to intimation.
vsm2.20:31.8:
The nineteen consciousnesses, namely, the ten life-continuum consciousnesses in the sense sphere ((41)–(49),
(56)), the five in the fine-material sphere ((57)–(61)), the three mind elements ((39), (55), (70)),
vsm2.20:31.9:
and the one resultant mind-consciousness element without root-cause and accompanied by joy (40),
give rise to materiality only, not to postures or to intimation.
vsm2.20:31.10:
The sixteen consciousnesses, namely, the two sets of five consciousnesses ((34)–(38), (50)–(54)),
the rebirth-linking consciousness of all beings, the death consciousness of those whose cankers are destroyed,
vsm2.20:31.11: and the four immaterial resultant consciousnesses ((62)–(65)) do not give rise to materiality or to postures or to intimation.
vsm2.20:31.12:
And those herein that do give rise to materiality do not do so at the instant of their presence
or at the instant of their dissolution, for consciousness is weak then.
vsm2.20:31.13:
But it is strong at the instant of arising. Consequently it originates materiality
then with the prenascent physical basis as its support.
vsm2.20:32.1:
(2) What is originated by consciousness is the three other immaterial aggregates and the seventeenfold materiality, namely, the
sound ennead, bodily intimation, verbal intimation, the space element, lightness, malleability, wieldiness, growth, and continuity.
vsm2.20:32.2:
(3) What has consciousness as its condition is the materiality of fourfold origination stated thus: “Postnascent states
of consciousness and consciousness-concomitants are a condition, as postnascence condition, for this prenascent body” (Paṭṭh I 5).
vsm2.20:33.1:
(4) What is originated by nutriment that has consciousness as its condition: the nutritive essence
that has reached presence in consciousness-originated material instances originates a
vsm2.20:33.2: further octad-with-nutritive-essence-as-eighth, and thus links up two or three occurrences of octads.
vsm2.20:34.1:
(5) What is originated by temperature that has consciousness as its condition:
the consciousness-originated temperature that has reached presence originates a further
vsm2.20:34.2: octad-with-nutritive-essence-as-eighth, and thus links up two or three occurrences.
vsm2.20:34.3: This is how the generation of consciousness-born materiality should be seen.
vsm2.20:35.1:
(C) NUTRIMENT-BORN MATERIALITY

Also as regards the nutriment-born kinds, the analysis should be understood thus: (1) nutriment,
vsm2.20:35.3: (3) what has nutriment as its condition,
vsm2.20:35.4: (4) what is originated by nutriment that has nutriment as its condition,
vsm2.20:35.5: (5) what is originated by temperature that has nutriment as its condition.
vsm2.20:36.2:
(2) What is originated by nutriment is the fourteenfold materiality, namely, (i–viii)
that of the octad-with-nutritive-essence-as-eighth originated by nutritive essence that has reached presence by obtaining
as its condition kamma-born materiality that is clung to (kammically acquired) and basing itself on that,
vsm2.20:36.3: and (ix) space element, (x–xiv) lightness, malleability, wieldiness, growth, and continuity.
vsm2.20:36.4:
(3) What has nutriment as its condition is the materiality of fourfold origination stated thus:
“Physical nutriment is a condition, as nutriment condition, for this body” (Paṭṭh I 5).
vsm2.20:37.1:
(4) What is originated by nutriment that has nutriment as its condition: the nutritive essence
that has reached presence in nutriment-originated material instances originates a further
vsm2.20:37.2:
octad-with-nutritive-essence-as-eighth and the nutritive essence in that octad originates a further
octad, and thus links up the occurrence of octads ten or twelve times.
vsm2.20:37.3: Nutriment taken on one day sustains for as long as seven days;
vsm2.20:37.4: but divine nutritive essence sustains for as long as one or two months.
vsm2.20:37.5: The nutriment taken by a mother originates materiality by pervading the body of the child in gestation.
vsm2.20:37.6: Also nutriment smeared on the body originates materiality.
vsm2.20:37.7: Kamma-born nutriment is a name for nutriment that is clung to.
vsm2.20:37.8:
That also originates materiality when it has reached presence. And the nutritive essence in it
originates a further octad. Thus it links up four or five occurrences.
vsm2.20:38.1:
(5) What is originated by temperature that has nutriment as its condition: nutriment-originated fire element
that has reached presence originates an octad-with-nutritive-essence-as-eighth that is thus temperature-originated.
vsm2.20:38.2: Here this nutriment is a condition for nutriment-originated material instances as their progenitor.
vsm2.20:38.3:
It is a condition for the rest as support, nutriment, presence, and non-disappearance.
This is how the generation of nutriment-born materiality should be seen.
vsm2.20:39.1:
(D) TEMPERATURE-BORN MATERIALITY

Also as regards the temperature-born kinds, the analysis should be understood thus: (1) temperature,
vsm2.20:39.3: (3) what has temperature as its condition,
vsm2.20:39.4: (4) what is originated by temperature that has temperature as its condition,
vsm2.20:39.5: (5) what is originated by nutriment that has temperature as its condition.
vsm2.20:40.1: Herein, (1) temperature is the fire element of fourfold origination; but it is twofold as hot temperature and cold temperature.
vsm2.20:40.2:
(2) What is originated by temperature: the temperature of fourfold origination that has reached
presence by obtaining a clung-to condition originates materiality in the body.
vsm2.20:40.3: That materiality is fifteenfold, namely, sound ennead, space element, lightness, malleability, wieldiness, growth, continuity.
vsm2.20:40.4:
(3) What has temperature as its condition is so called since temperature
is a condition for the occurrence and for the destruction of materiality of fourfold origination.
vsm2.20:41.1:
(4) What is originated by temperature that has temperature as its condition:
the temperature-originated fire element that has reached presence originates a further
octad-with-nutritive-essence-as-eighth, and the temperature in that octad originates a further octad.
vsm2.20:41.2:
Thus temperature-originated materiality both goes on occurring for a long period and also
maintains itself as well in what is not clung to.
vsm2.20:42.1:
(5) What is originated by nutriment that has temperature as its condition: the temperature-originated nutritive
essence that has reached presence originates a further octad-with-nutritive-essence-as-eighth,
vsm2.20:42.2: and the nutritive essence in that originates a further one, thus it links up ten or twelve occurrences of octads.
vsm2.20:42.3: Herein, this temperature is a condition for temperature-originated material instances as their progenitor.
vsm2.20:42.4:
It is a condition for the rest as support, presence, and non-disappearance.
This is how the generation of temperature-born materiality should be seen.
vsm2.20:42.5: One who sees the generation of materiality thus is said to “comprehend the material at one time” (§21).
